claim_verdicts.evidence: index.md:14: "EF Core compares the current model against a snapshot of the old model to determine the differences, and generates migration source files; the files can be tracked in your project's source control like any other source file." index.md:114: "the model snapshot is one of the files generated by EF Core when you add a migration, and is checked into source control". applying.md:156-159: "The following updates your database to the latest migration: `dotnet ef database update`". The lesson's diff base ("a snapshot of that model as it was at the last migration") matches.

applying.md:397-399 ("Apply migrations at runtime"): "It's possible for the application itself to apply migrations programmatically, typically during startup." applying.md:409-423: "To apply migrations programmatically, call `context.Database.MigrateAsync()`", with an ASP.NET sample calling it once inside `using (var scope = host.Services.CreateScope())` after Build(). applying.md:27 lists "Runtime migration" beside the CLI strategies for the same job. Program.cs at stage-1 (lines 57-62) uses the sync `Migrate()` in exactly that shape.

history-table.md:10-11: "By default, EF Core keeps track of which migrations have been applied to the database by recording them in a table named `__EFMigrationsHistory`." managing.md:329-336 ("Resetting all migrations") describes marking a migration applied by hand: "delete all rows from the migrations history table" ... "INSERT INTO [__EFMigrationsHistory] ([MIGRATIONID], [PRODUCTVERSION]) VALUES (N'<full_migration_timestamp_and_name>', N'<EF_version>');" — the same two columns and technique MigrationBaseline uses.

MigrationBaseline.cs:16-40 at stage-1: `if (historyCheck.ExecuteScalar() is not DBNull) return;` after `SELECT to_regclass('public."__EFMigrationsHistory"')::text`; `if (tablesCheck.ExecuteScalar() is DBNull) return;` after `SELECT to_regclass('public.customers')::text`; then CommandText = CREATE TABLE "__EFMigrationsHistory" (MigrationId varchar(150) NOT NULL, ProductVersion varchar(32) NOT NULL, PK) + INSERT ... VALUES ('20260923154631_InitialCreate', '10.0.4'); ExecuteNonQuery(). Lines 41-46 are only try/finally + connection.Close(); no migration is executed.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Program.cs` lines 52-62: `var app = builder.Build();` then `using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope()) { var context = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<DonHangDbContext>(); MigrationBaseline.ApplyIfNeeded(context); context.Database.Migrate(); }`; only afterwards `app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>()`, `UseCors()`, `UseAuthentication()`, `MapControllers()`, `app.Run()`. One call, immediately before Migrate(), before any middleware.

`git show stage-1:.../20260923154700_AddPasswordHashToCustomers.cs` lines 13-35: Up = AddColumn<string>(name: "password_hash", table: "customers", type: "text", nullable: true) then migrationBuilder.Sql("UPDATE customers SET password_hash = '100000.O2f9...' WHERE id IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5);"); Down = DropColumn(name: "password_hash", table: "customers"). db/seed.sql at stage-1 inserts customers with ids 1-5 — exactly 5 rows, so "all 5 seeded customers" holds.

Live this session: `docker exec donhang-db psql -U donhang -d donhang -c 'select "MigrationId","ProductVersion" from "__EFMigrationsHistory" order by "MigrationId";'` -> 20260923154631_InitialCreate | 10.0.4; 20260923154700_AddPasswordHashToCustomers | 10.0.4; 20260924092625_AddOrderCustomerNavigation | 10.0.4; (3 rows). `git ls-tree --name-only stage-1 DonHang.Infrastructure/Migrations/` lists 7 files: those 3 .cs, 3 matching .Designer.cs, and DonHangDbContextModelSnapshot.cs.
claim_verdicts.source: live psql run on the stage-1 lab; git ls-tree stage-1

claim_verdicts.evidence: InitialCreate.cs at stage-1 calls CreateTable for customers (l.15-16), notifications (30-31), orders (46-47), payments (61-62), products (77-78), order_items (91-92) — the same tables db/schema.sql creates. Live on the stage-1 lab db: `BEGIN; CREATE TABLE customers (id int); ROLLBACK;` -> `ERROR:  relation "customers" already exists`. So InitialCreate's CreateTable step cannot succeed there. (The end-to-end Migrate() failure itself was not re-run; the failing statement was.)

claim_verdicts.evidence: index.md:61: "EF Core will create a directory called **Migrations** in your project, and generate some files. It's a good idea to inspect what exactly EF Core generated - and possibly amend it - but we'll skip over that for now." The repo shows such an amendment: AddPasswordHashToCustomers.cs:19-26 carries a hand-written comment block ("// lesson: backend.l1.hashing-passwords ... obviously-fake dev password") above migrationBuilder.Sql(...), next to the generated AddColumn call.

Claim added in this same round-2 pass, using this reviewer's own already-gathered evidence: the section-5 major issue already ran `select to_regclass('public."__EFMigrationsHistory"')::text, to_regclass('public.customers')::text, to_regclass('public.nosuch')::text;` live on the stage-1 lab, returning the quoted identifier, `customers`, and NULL respectively — NULL surfaces to C# as DBNull via ExecuteScalar, matching MigrationBaseline's `is DBNull`/`is not DBNull` checks.

issues.text: The definition rules out what the lesson itself then shows. Section 5's example migration ends with `migrationBuilder.Sql("UPDATE customers SET password_hash = ... WHERE id IN (1,2,3,4,5);")` — a change to the rows in the table — and section 4 calls it "a hand-written backfill (an `UPDATE` filling a new column on rows that already exist)". EF docs agree: operations.md:14 "Use `MigrationBuilder.Sql()` for transformations that calculate values from existing database rows"; managing.md:16 cites "Data operations ... inserting, updating, deleting, and transforming data in migrations".
issues.fix: Rewrite the clause without the absolute: "**migration** — a versioned, code-tracked description of one schema change: a change to the tables and columns themselves rather than to the data in them, though a migration can also carry SQL that fills in rows, as one in this lesson does." Leave the misconception bullet ("it has nothing to do with backing up or restoring data") unchanged — that one is correct.
issues.quote: one change to the tables and columns themselves, not to the rows stored in them

issues.text: Unlisted claim: the behaviour of PostgreSQL's `to_regclass` and its mapping to `DBNull` is asserted in prose but is nowhere in `.meta.json` claims (claim 4 covers only ApplyIfNeeded's control flow), and `versions_used` lists `efcore` alone although this is PostgreSQL-specific behaviour. It is also imprecise: run live on the stage-1 db, `select to_regclass('public."__EFMigrationsHistory"')::text, to_regclass('public.customers')::text, to_regclass('public.nosuch')::text;` returns `"__EFMigrationsHistory"` (with the quotes, since that identifier needs them), `customers`, and NULL.
issues.fix: Add a claim to `.meta.json` (kind `behavior`, section 5, version_key `postgresql`): "to_regclass('<table>')::text returns the relation's identifier when it exists and NULL when it does not; ADO.NET surfaces that NULL as DBNull.Value from ExecuteScalar", source = PostgreSQL 17 system information functions + the psql run; add `postgresql` to `versions_used`. Optionally write "returns a name for the table when it exists" instead of "the table's name".
issues.quote: Each `to_regclass` query below returns the table's name when the table exists, and `null` — `DBNull` in C# — when it does not
